filing-returns/xbrl-filing.title: XBRL Filing
filing-returns/xbrl-filing.html:
XBRL Filing: A Comprehensive Overview

Introduction

XBRL (Extensible Business Reporting Language) is a standardized format for electronically reporting business and financial information. It improves the consistency, accuracy, and usability of financial data and is used by regulators and businesses in various jurisdictions, including India.

What is XBRL?

XBRL is an XML-based framework that uses standardized tags to identify and classify financial information. It enables financial data to be processed, analyzed, and compared more efficiently while reducing manual intervention.

Importance of XBRL Filing

  1. Standardized Reporting: Makes financial information consistent and easier to compare.
  2. Improved Efficiency: Reduces manual data entry and streamlines reporting.
  3. Better Accuracy: Structured tagging helps improve data quality and reduce reporting errors.
  4. Regulatory Compliance: Helps applicable entities meet prescribed XBRL filing requirements.
  5. Better Data Analysis: Makes financial information easier for regulators and stakeholders to process and analyze.
  6. Cost Savings: Automation can reduce time and effort involved in financial reporting.

XBRL Filing Process

  1. Prepare Financial Data: Organize financial information according to the applicable requirements.
  2. Apply XBRL Tags: Map financial items to the appropriate taxonomy elements.
  3. Validate Data: Check the file for tagging, calculation, and other filing errors.
  4. Generate XBRL File: Prepare the final file in the required format.
  5. Submit Filing: Upload the file through the applicable regulatory portal.
  6. Review & Correction: Address any errors or validation issues and re-submit where required.

Challenges in XBRL Filing

  • Technical Complexity: Requires knowledge of XBRL taxonomies and filing requirements.
  • Accurate Tagging: Incorrect mapping can affect the quality of the filing.
  • System Integration: May require integration with accounting or financial reporting systems.
  • Regulatory Changes: Taxonomies and filing requirements may change, requiring regular updates.

licenses/brn-registration.title: BRN Registration
licenses/brn-registration.html:
BRN Registration: A Complete Guide

What is BRN Registration?

A Business Registration Number (BRN) is a unique identification number issued by the relevant government authority to identify a registered business. It may be used for taxation, regulatory compliance, official records, and business transactions, depending on the applicable jurisdiction.

Why is BRN Registration Important?

  • Legal Recognition: Provides official recognition of the business.
  • Tax Compliance: Supports applicable tax and regulatory requirements.
  • Banking & Finance: May be required for business banking and financial services.
  • Business Credibility: Helps establish trust with customers, vendors, and institutions.
  • Government Benefits: May support access to eligible government schemes and incentives.
  • Contracts & Tenders: Can be required for certain tenders, contracts, and commercial transactions.

Who May Need BRN Registration?

Requirements vary by jurisdiction and business structure. It may apply to:

  • Sole proprietorships
  • Partnerships
  • Private limited companies
  • Limited liability partnerships (LLPs)
  • Non-profit organizations
  • Other businesses engaged in commercial activities

Documents Required

Commonly required documents may include:

  • Owner's identity and PAN proof
  • Business address proof
  • Incorporation certificate, where applicable
  • Partnership deed or LLP agreement, where applicable
  • MoA and AoA for companies
  • GST registration details, where applicable

BRN Registration Process

  1. Check Requirements – Determine whether BRN registration applies to the business.
  2. Prepare Documents – Collect documents based on the business structure.
  3. Submit Application – Apply through the relevant government authority or portal.
  4. Pay Applicable Fees – Complete the prescribed fee payment, where applicable.
  5. Verification – Authorities review the application and supporting documents.
  6. BRN Issuance – Receive the Business Registration Number upon approval.

Processing Time

Processing time depends on the jurisdiction, business type, and verification requirements. Applications may take several business days or longer where additional verification is required.

Consequences of Non-Compliance

Where BRN registration is mandatory, failure to register may result in penalties, compliance issues, or difficulties with certain banking, licensing, government, or commercial activities.

Renewal & Updates

Where applicable, businesses must renew their registration periodically and update authorities about changes such as business address, ownership, or business structure.

licenses/food-license-registration.title: Food License Registration
licenses/food-license-registration.html:
Food License Registration: A Complete Guide

FSSAI Registration/License is required for businesses involved in the manufacture, processing, storage, distribution, sale, or handling of food products in India, as applicable under food safety regulations. Issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), it helps businesses meet prescribed food safety and hygiene standards while building consumer confidence.

Types of FSSAI Registration/License

FSSAI registration or licensing generally depends on the nature, scale, and turnover of the food business:

  1. Basic FSSAI Registration: Generally applicable to small food businesses with annual turnover up to ₹12 lakh, subject to applicable criteria.
  2. State FSSAI License: Generally applicable to food businesses operating within a state that exceed the basic registration threshold and fall within the prescribed criteria.
  3. Central FSSAI License: Generally required for businesses falling under central licensing criteria, including certain large-scale businesses, importers, exporters, and specified food operators.

Who Needs FSSAI Registration/License?

It may be required for:

  • Food manufacturers and processors
  • Restaurants, cafés, caterers, and cloud kitchens
  • Food retailers, traders, and wholesalers
  • Home-based food businesses
  • Food importers and exporters
  • Dairy, meat, and other food processing units
  • Food storage and distribution businesses

Documents Required

Depending on the type and nature of the business, commonly required documents include:

  • Identity and address proof of the applicant
  • Business registration or constitution documents
  • Proof of business premises
  • Passport-size photograph
  • List of food products and business activities
  • Layout plan and machinery details, where applicable
  • Water testing report for relevant manufacturing businesses
  • Details of directors/partners and other prescribed documents

Steps to Apply for FSSAI Registration/License

  1. Determine the Applicable Category: Identify the registration or licence required based on your business activities and scale.
  2. Prepare Documents: Gather the required information and supporting documents.
  3. Submit Online Application: Apply through the official FSSAI licensing portal.
  4. Pay Applicable Fees: Submit the prescribed government fee.
  5. Inspection and Verification: An inspection may be conducted where required.
  6. License Issuance: Once the application meets the applicable requirements, the FSSAI registration or licence is issued.

Benefits of FSSAI Registration/License

  • Legal Compliance: Helps meet applicable food safety requirements.
  • Consumer Trust: Builds confidence in the safety and quality of food products.
  • Business Credibility: Strengthens the reputation of the food business.
  • Market Expansion: Supports business growth and entry into wider markets.
  • Quality Assurance: Promotes compliance with prescribed food safety and hygiene standards.

licenses/gst-registration.title: GST Registration
licenses/gst-registration.html:
GST Registration with Taxswami: A Complete Guide

GST (Goods and Services Tax) is an indirect tax applicable to the supply of goods and services in India. GST registration is required for businesses crossing the prescribed thresholds or falling under specific categories covered by GST law.

Who Needs GST Registration?

GST registration may be required for:

  1. Businesses whose turnover exceeds the applicable threshold.
  2. Persons making supplies covered by compulsory registration provisions, including certain inter-state suppliers.
  3. E-commerce operators and specified e-commerce sellers.
  4. Casual and non-resident taxable persons.
  5. Persons liable to pay tax under the reverse charge mechanism.
  6. Input Service Distributors and other persons covered under compulsory registration provisions.

Benefits of GST Registration

  1. Legal Compliance: Enables businesses to operate in accordance with applicable GST requirements.
  2. Input Tax Credit: Eligible businesses can claim credit for GST paid on qualifying purchases and expenses.
  3. Business Credibility: GST registration can enhance credibility with customers, suppliers, and business partners.
  4. Business Expansion: Facilitates taxable transactions across different states, subject to applicable rules.
  5. Simplified Tax Structure: GST provides a unified framework for indirect taxation across India.

Documents Required for GST Registration

  • PAN and Aadhaar of the proprietor, partners, or directors
  • Business address proof, such as utility bill, rent agreement, or ownership document
  • Bank account details, where applicable
  • Photograph of the proprietor, partners, or authorised persons
  • Business incorporation certificate, partnership deed, or other constitution documents
  • Digital signature, where required

GST Registration Process with Taxswami

  1. Application: Submit the GST registration application with the required details and documents.
  2. TRN Generation: A Temporary Reference Number (TRN) is generated for tracking the application.
  3. Document Verification: The application and submitted information are reviewed by the tax authorities.
  4. ARN Generation: An Application Reference Number (ARN) is issued after successful submission.
  5. GSTIN Allocation: Upon approval, a unique GST Identification Number (GSTIN) is issued.

Types of GST Registration

  1. Normal Taxpayer: For businesses registered under the regular GST scheme.
  2. Casual Taxable Person: For persons making taxable supplies occasionally without a fixed place of business.
  3. Composition Taxpayer: A simplified scheme available to eligible small taxpayers subject to prescribed conditions and limits.
  4. Non-Resident Taxable Person: For non-residents making taxable supplies in India without a fixed place of business in India.

Import Export Code (IEC): A Complete Guide

The Import Export Code (IEC) is an essential requirement for businesses involved in international trade in India. Issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), IEC helps businesses comply with applicable import and export regulations and conduct cross-border trade smoothly.

What is Import Export Code (IEC)?

IEC is a unique identification number issued by the DGFT to eligible businesses and individuals engaged in import or export activities. It is generally required for customs clearance and other import-export transactions, subject to applicable exemptions.

Who Needs an IEC?

IEC may be required by:

  • Importers purchasing goods from overseas markets.
  • Exporters supplying goods to international customers.

Why Choose Taxswami for IEC Registration?

  • Online Support: Complete assistance without unnecessary paperwork or visits.

In a competitive market, businesses need to build credibility, improve efficiency, and follow recognized quality standards. ISO certification helps organizations establish structured management systems and demonstrate their commitment to quality, safety, security, and efficiency.

ISO develops internationally recognized standards for quality, safety, efficiency, and management systems across various industries. ISO certification indicates that an organization’s processes meet the requirements of a specific ISO standard, subject to assessment by an appropriate certification body.

Types of ISO Certifications

  1. ISO 9001: Quality Management System focused on consistent quality and customer satisfaction.
  2. ISO 14001: Environmental Management System focused on managing environmental impact.
  3. ISO 27001: Information Security Management System focused on protecting information and managing security risks.

licenses/rera-registration-in-india.html:
RERA Registration in India: A Complete Guide

The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA) was introduced to promote transparency, accountability, and efficiency in India’s real estate sector. RERA registration is required for eligible real estate projects and agents, helping establish a regulated framework and protect the interests of homebuyers. Taxswami assists developers, builders, and agents with the registration process.

What is RERA?

RERA provides a regulatory framework for the real estate sector and aims to improve transparency in property transactions. It requires eligible projects and agents to comply with prescribed disclosure, registration, and regulatory requirements.

Who Needs RERA Registration?

  1. Real Estate Developers/Promoters: Eligible projects, generally including those exceeding 500 sq. metres or having more than 8 apartments, must be registered, subject to applicable exemptions.
  2. Real Estate Agents: Agents facilitating the sale or purchase of properties in registered projects generally require registration with the respective state RERA authority.
  3. Certain Ongoing Projects: Projects meeting the applicable criteria and not having received a completion certificate may also require registration.

Documents Required for RERA Registration

For Builders/Developers:

  • PAN and business/entity documents
  • Land ownership and title documents
  • Project plans, approvals, and development details
  • Project timelines and financial information
  • Details of architects, engineers, and contractors

For Real Estate Agents:

  • PAN and identity proof
  • Business and office address proof
  • Business/entity documents, where applicable
  • Other documents prescribed by the respective state RERA authority

RERA Registration Process

  1. State RERA Portal: Identify the applicable state RERA authority and portal.
  2. Application Filing: Submit the required project or agent details.
  3. Document Submission: Upload the prescribed supporting documents.
  4. Fee Payment: Pay the applicable registration fee.
  5. Verification & Approval: The authority reviews the application and, upon approval, issues the RERA registration number.

Benefits of RERA Registration

  • Greater Transparency: Promotes disclosure of project details, approvals, timelines, and other prescribed information.
  • Buyer Protection: Provides a regulatory framework and mechanisms for addressing eligible buyer grievances.
  • Regulatory Compliance: Helps developers and agents meet applicable legal requirements.
  • Industry Credibility: Encourages more structured and transparent real estate practices.

licenses/shop-act-registration.title: Shop Act Registration
licenses/shop-act-registration.html:
Shop Act Registration: A Complete Guide

Introduction

Shop Act Registration is a mandatory registration for businesses operating under the Shops and Establishments Act applicable in each state. It regulates working conditions, employee welfare, and business operations while providing legal recognition to commercial establishments.

What is Shop Act Registration?

Shop Act Registration is a state-specific registration required for shops, offices, and commercial establishments. It covers matters such as working hours, wages, leave policies, and employee rights, ensuring compliance with applicable labour laws.

Who Needs Shop Act Registration?

The registration is generally required for:

  • Retail and wholesale shops
  • Offices, consultancies, and service businesses
  • Hotels, restaurants, and cafés
  • Educational institutions and commercial establishments
  • Warehouses and storage units

Benefits of Shop Act Registration

  • Legal Recognition: Establishes the business as a registered entity.
  • Labour Law Compliance: Helps meet applicable employment and workplace regulations.
  • Banking Support: Often accepted as business address proof for opening bank accounts.
  • Business Credibility: Enhances trust among customers, suppliers, and financial institutions.
  • Access to Benefits: May support applications for licenses, registrations, and certain government schemes.

Documents Required

The documents required may vary by state, but generally include:

  • Aadhaar and PAN of the owner or authorized person
  • Business address proof (electricity bill, rent agreement, etc.)
  • Passport-size photograph
  • Details of employees, where applicable
  • Business establishment information

Registration Process

  1. Application Filing: Submit the application through the respective state portal or authority.
  2. Document Submission: Upload the required documents.
  3. Fee Payment: Pay the prescribed registration fee.
  4. Verification: Authorities verify the details and documents.
  5. Certificate Issuance: The registration certificate is issued upon approval.

Validity and Renewal

The validity period varies from state to state and may range from one to five years. Renewal, where applicable, should be completed before expiry to maintain compliance.

Penalties for Non-Compliance

Failure to obtain or renew Shop Act Registration may lead to penalties, fines, or other legal consequences under the applicable state laws.

licenses/start-up-registration.title: Start-up Registration
licenses/start-up-registration.html:
Startup Registration: A Comprehensive Guide

Introduction

Starting a business involves choosing the right legal structure, completing applicable registrations, and meeting regulatory requirements. In India, eligible businesses can also apply for DPIIT Startup Recognition to access certain government benefits and support.

What is Startup Registration?

Startup registration generally involves establishing a business as a company, LLP, or other suitable entity and, where eligible, obtaining recognition under the DPIIT Startup India initiative.

DPIIT recognition is separate from basic business incorporation and may provide eligible startups access to certain tax benefits, intellectual property support, funding programs, and regulatory benefits.

Benefits of Startup Registration

  • Legal Recognition: Establishes the business under the applicable legal structure.
  • Funding Opportunities: Eligible startups may access government-backed funding programs and other financing opportunities.
  • Tax Benefits: Recognized startups may qualify for specific tax benefits subject to applicable conditions.
  • Limited Liability: Companies and LLPs can provide limited liability protection, subject to their legal structure.
  • Business Credibility: Formal registration can strengthen credibility with customers, investors, and partners.
  • IPR Support: Eligible startups may receive support and benefits for patents, trademarks, and other intellectual property.

Business Structures for Startups

  1. Sole Proprietorship – Simple structure owned and operated by one individual, but without separate legal identity.
  2. Partnership – Two or more persons share ownership and responsibilities under a partnership arrangement.
  3. LLP – Combines partnership flexibility with limited liability and separate legal identity.
  4. Private Limited Company – Separate legal entity with limited liability and a structure suitable for raising investment.
  5. Public Limited Company – Generally suited to larger businesses seeking to raise capital from the public.

Startup Registration Process

  1. Choose a Business Structure – Select the structure based on ownership, liability, funding, and business needs.
  2. Choose a Business Name – Select a compliant and available name.
  3. Incorporate the Business – Complete the applicable registration with the relevant authority, such as the MCA.
  4. Obtain Required Registrations – Apply for GST, FSSAI, trade licenses, or other registrations where applicable.
  5. Apply for DPIIT Recognition – Eligible businesses can apply for recognition under the Startup India framework.
  6. Open a Business Bank Account – Set up a dedicated account for business transactions.
  7. Maintain Compliance – Complete applicable tax, statutory, and regulatory filings.

trade-patent/copyright-registration.title: Copyright Registration

Copyright Registration in India

Copyright protects original creative works such as literary, artistic, musical, and software works. In India, copyright generally arises automatically when an original work is created; registration is not mandatory for protection but provides an official record of the claimed ownership and details of the work.

Taxswami assists individuals, creators, and businesses with the copyright registration process and related documentation.

Why is Copyright Registration Important?

  1. Evidence of Ownership: Registration provides an official record of the copyright claim and particulars of the work.
  2. Protection Against Unauthorized Use: Copyright gives the owner statutory rights over specified uses of the work.
  3. Commercial Opportunities: Copyright can be licensed, assigned, or commercially exploited.
  4. Infringement Support: Registration records can be useful in enforcing rights and resolving disputes.
  5. Business Value: Copyright can form part of a business's intellectual property portfolio.

What Can Be Protected by Copyright?

Copyright protection may apply to original works including:

  • Books, articles, manuscripts, and other literary works
  • Music, lyrics, and sound recordings
  • Films and audiovisual works
  • Computer software and certain digital works
  • Paintings, drawings, photographs, and other artistic works
  • Architectural works
  • Choreographic and other eligible creative works
  • Websites and other original digital content, where eligible

Copyright protects the expression of an idea, rather than the underlying idea, concept, method, or principle itself.

Copyright Registration Process

1. Determine Eligibility

Review the work to determine whether it falls within a protected category and satisfies applicable requirements.

2. Prepare Documents

The application generally requires details of the applicant, author, nature of the work, title, and a copy or representation of the work, along with other documents where applicable.

3. File the Application

The application is submitted to the Copyright Office in the prescribed form, along with the applicable government fee.

4. Examination and Objections

The application undergoes the prescribed process. Where objections or discrepancies arise, the applicant may be required to provide clarification or supporting documents.

5. Registration

If the application meets the applicable requirements and no unresolved objection prevents registration, the work is entered in the Register of Copyrights and the registration certificate is issued.

trade-patent/design-registration.title: Design Registration
trade-patent/design-registration.html:
Design Registration in India

A registered design protects the visual features of a product, helping businesses, manufacturers, and designers safeguard the appearance of their products from unauthorized copying. In India, design registration is governed by the Designs Act, 2000 and the applicable Designs Rules.

What is Design Registration?

Design registration protects the visual features of an article, including its shape, configuration, pattern, ornamentation, or composition of lines or colours, as applied to an article. Registration gives the proprietor statutory protection against unauthorized application of the registered design, subject to applicable law.

Benefits of Design Registration

  1. Legal Protection: Provides statutory protection for the registered design.
  2. Competitive Advantage: Helps prevent unauthorized copying of the product's visual appearance.
  3. Business Value: A registered design is an intellectual property asset that may be assigned or licensed.
  4. Evidence of Rights: Registration provides official evidence of the proprietor's rights.
  5. Encourages Innovation: Protects original product designs and supports creative development.
  6. Brand Differentiation: Helps businesses distinguish their products through distinctive visual designs.

Eligibility for Design Registration

A design generally must:

  • Be New or Original: It should not have been previously published or used in the relevant manner before the filing/priority date.
  • Have Distinctive Visual Features: The design should relate to the visual appearance of the article.
  • Be Applied to an Article: It must be applied to an article capable of industrial or manufacturing production.
  • Be Visible to the Eye: Protection relates to visual features of the article and not merely its functional or mechanical features.
  • Meet Statutory Requirements: The design must not fall within the exclusions under the Designs Act, 2000.

Design Registration Process

1. Design Search and Consultation

A preliminary search and review helps assess whether the design appears eligible and sufficiently distinctive.

2. Application Preparation and Filing

The application is prepared with the required representations, applicant details, statement of novelty, classification, and other prescribed information.

3. Examination

The Controller of Designs examines the application. If objections are raised, the applicant may submit a response or make permitted amendments.

4. Registration and Publication

Once the application satisfies the applicable requirements, the design is registered and details are published in the Official Journal.

5. Registration Certificate

A certificate of registration is issued to the registered proprietor.

Validity of Design Registration

Design registration in India is initially valid for 10 years from the date of registration and may generally be extended once for an additional 5 years, subject to the prescribed requirements and fee.

trade-patent/patent-registration.title: Patent Registration
trade-patent/patent-registration.html:
Patent Registration in India

A patent is a statutory right granted for an invention that meets the requirements of patentability under applicable law. In India, a patent can protect a new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application.

Patent protection can help inventors and businesses prevent unauthorized commercial use and create opportunities for licensing, assignment, and commercialization.

Importance of Patent Registration

Patent registration can help:

  • Protect inventions from unauthorized commercial exploitation.
  • Establish legal rights over the patented invention.
  • Create licensing and commercialization opportunities.
  • Enhance the commercial value and credibility of an innovation.
  • Support business growth and attract potential investors.

Benefits of Patent Registration

  1. Exclusive Rights: The patent holder can prevent others from making, using, selling, offering for sale, or importing the patented invention in India, subject to applicable law.
  2. Protection Against Infringement: Provides legal remedies against unauthorized use of the patented invention.
  3. Monetization: Patents can be licensed, assigned, or commercially exploited.
  4. Business Value: Patented technology can strengthen a company's intellectual property portfolio.
  5. Competitive Advantage: Patent protection can support commercialization of innovative products and processes.

Patent Eligibility in India

For an invention to be patentable, it generally must satisfy the following requirements:

  • Novelty: The invention must be new and not already publicly disclosed.
  • Inventive Step: It must involve a technical advance or economic significance and not be obvious to a person skilled in the art.
  • Industrial Applicability: It must be capable of being made or used in industry.
  • Patentable Subject Matter: The invention must not fall within the exclusions under the Patents Act, 1970.

Patent Validity in India

A patent granted in India generally remains in force for 20 years from the date of filing the patent application, subject to payment of the prescribed renewal fees and other applicable requirements.

After the patent term expires, the invention enters the public domain and the patent rights cease.

Patent Registration Process

1. Patent Search and Analysis

A prior-art search is conducted to assess the novelty and patentability of the invention and identify potential conflicts.

2. Patent Application Drafting

A patent specification is prepared with the required description, claims, abstract, and drawings, where applicable. Depending on the stage of development, a provisional or complete specification may be filed.

3. Filing the Application

The application is filed with the Indian Patent Office along with the prescribed forms and government fees.

4. Publication

Patent applications are ordinarily published after 18 months from the filing or priority date, subject to applicable provisions and requests for early publication.

5. Examination

The applicant must request examination within the prescribed period. The Patent Office examines the application and may issue objections requiring a response or amendments.

6. Grant of Patent

If the application satisfies the applicable legal requirements and examination objections are resolved, the patent is granted and the grant is published by the Patent Office.

trade-patent/trade-mark-registration.title: Trade Mark Registration
trade-patent/trade-mark-registration.html:
Trademark Registration in India

A trademark is a word, name, logo, symbol, design, or combination that distinguishes the goods or services of one business from those of others. Registration provides statutory protection and helps the owner establish exclusive rights over the mark for the registered goods or services.

Importance of Trademark Registration

  1. Legal Protection: Provides statutory rights against unauthorized use of the registered mark.
  2. Exclusive Rights: Gives the owner exclusive rights to use the mark for the registered goods or services, subject to applicable law.
  3. Brand Recognition: Helps customers identify and distinguish a business and its products or services.
  4. Business Asset: A registered trademark is an intangible asset that can be licensed, assigned, or commercially exploited.
  5. Protection Against Confusion: Helps prevent unauthorized use of identical or deceptively similar marks in relevant circumstances.

Trademark Registration Process in India

Trademark registration is governed by the Trade Marks Act, 1999 and administered by the Trade Marks Registry under the Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trade Marks (CGPDTM).

1. Trademark Search

A search is conducted to identify existing identical or similar marks and assess potential conflicts before filing.

2. Application Filing

The application can be filed online through the IP India portal. It generally includes:

  • Applicant details
  • Wordmark or logo
  • Description of goods/services
  • Applicable trademark class under the Nice Classification
  • Power of attorney, where filed through an agent or attorney

3. Examination

The Registrar examines the application under the Trade Marks Act. If objections are raised, an Examination Report is issued and the applicant may submit a response.

4. Publication and Opposition

If the application is accepted, it is published in the Trade Marks Journal to allow third parties to oppose the registration. The statutory opposition period is four months from publication.

5. Registration

If no opposition is filed, or any opposition is resolved in the applicant's favour, the trademark is registered and a registration certificate is issued.

A registered trademark is generally valid for 10 years from the date of application and can be renewed indefinitely for further 10-year periods.

Documents Required

  • Trademark logo or wordmark, where applicable
  • Applicant's identity and address proof
  • Business/entity registration documents, where applicable
  • Details of goods/services
  • Power of attorney, where applicable
  • Other supporting documents depending on the applicant and application
